intro:
Transylvania's seat 1 (far left): drawn facing the viewer's right, as the game shows him. Built the way the Wolf Man is (`art-tools/pose_rig.py`). REDRAWN GOTHIC (the owner: "Gothic Style yes", from Transylvania on): he was built in the presidents' flat cartoon and is now the one flat figure among four gothic ones at his table. His first sheets are kept in `sources/old_style/`.

His look, from his character file and Stoker: square and solid, shoulders set back over a deep chest, clean-shaven, square-jawed, bushy brows, reddish hair swept back off a broad forehead, wide-set blue eyes, in a plain black professor's frock coat, his doctor's bag on the felt beside him (a prop by his left elbow). His prop is his spectacles; they are small, so the tell is the whole gesture: off, polished on a big white handkerchief, back on. A small silver crucifix at his collar carries the weak tell.

Ruled out (his character file): the 2004 Van Helsing film entirely (no broad-brimmed hat, no long leather coat, no crossbow, no gadgets) and the likeness of any actor who has played him. His Dutch is used lightly, never as a comic accent. Layout from Lancelot's character sheet, style from the Headless Horseman's character sheet.

Tags (MOTION-SPEC.md): his three tells, each beside the idle it hides among: taking off his spectacles and cleaning them (strong) beside writing a line in his leather diary (both hands busy, eyes down); touching the crucifix at his collar (weak) beside checking a pocket that smells of garlic (a hand to the coat); muttering in Dutch (tilted) beside sniffing the air, frowning (the face alone). 'Glances at the fireplace' is C4. B3 and D4 are the big win and the crushing loss; his hands are empty of cards and chips in every pose (the game moves them); knocked out, he says his line and fades from the chair.

character:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: Professor Abraham Van Helsing, of Bram Stoker's Dracula (1897), as Stoker describes him. Copy ONLY the LAYOUT of the FIRST attached sheet (what goes where): take NOTHING of its character. No plate armour, no gauntlets, no striped surcoat, no long hair. Take the STYLE from the SECOND attached image.

Van Helsing: a Dutch professor of medicine of about sixty, square and solid, shoulders set back over a deep chest; clean-shaven, square-jawed, with a firm, kindly mouth; big bushy reddish brows; reddish hair going grey, swept back off a broad, high forehead; wide-set blue eyes behind small round gold-rimmed spectacles; a plain black professor's frock coat over a dark waistcoat, a white shirt and a black cravat; a small silver crucifix on a short chain at his collar. Shrewd, warm, tireless, a little odd. His bag is a small black leather doctor's bag. NO broad-brimmed hat, NO long leather coat, NO crossbow, NO stakes, NO weapons, NO gadgets. Nothing from any film, and no likeness of any actor. His FACE: a bold dark outline, the age shown by a few firm lines (the brow, the corners of the eyes and mouth) and by the shading, never wrinkle by wrinkle. Black cloth with the warm candlelit rim light along the shoulders and sleeves, so the coat never reads as a flat black shape.

Pure white background (#FFFFFF). Every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches or overlaps. No text, no labels, no frames, no cast shadows.

The angle: a gentle three-quarter view, turned about 25 degrees from front-on, facing the viewer's right. Both eyes, the whole nose, the mouth and both shoulders clearly visible. NOT profile.

Draw, all facing the viewer's right, at the same size:
- Finished heads, each with the neck and the top of the collar and cravat: neutral, spectacles on; talking, mouth open mid-word, spectacles on; his spectacles OFF, eyes narrowed, a little short-sighted; muttering out of the side of his mouth, eyes sideways
- The torso in the frock coat, the crucifix at the collar: no head, cut off straight below the waist, the upper arms down to the elbows; NO forearms, NO hands
- Two forearms in the coat sleeves, white shirt cuffs showing, lying on a table, pointing toward its centre, open at the elbow end
- On their own: the small round gold-rimmed spectacles; a big white handkerchief; a small brown leather diary with a pencil; the small black leather doctor's bag, closed; a bulb of garlic
- Four seated reference poses, waist up behind the curved edge of a round green poker table, forearms resting on its edge, hands apart, the doctor's bag standing on the felt by his left elbow: neutral; holding his spectacles in one hand and polishing them with the white handkerchief in the other; two fingers of his right hand touching the crucifix at his collar; muttering aside

A: At rest: both forearms lying along the table's edge, his hands resting on the felt in front of him, a hand's width apart, relaxed and NOT touching, NOT laced, NOT overlapping; spectacles on; the black doctor's bag standing on the felt by his left elbow; a calm, shrewd look, mouth closed
Peeking at his cards: his right hand cupped low over the felt in front of him, thumb lifted a little, as if shielding something small; eyes down through his spectacles
Checking: two fingers of his right hand tapping the felt
Calling: his right hand flat, fingers leading, pushing forward along the felt
Betting: leaning in a little, his right hand pushed well forward along the felt, palm down, deliberate
Folding: a flat push of his right hand toward the middle of the table, palm down, a little regretful
B: All in: both hands pushing forward along the felt together, leaning in, eyes keen behind the spectacles
Showing: his right hand turning palm up from the felt, as if turning something over
A big win: both fists raised high, head back, laughing out loud, spectacles on, the bag still by his left elbow
Cleaning his spectacles: the spectacles OFF, held up in front of his chest in his left hand, his right hand polishing a lens with a big white handkerchief, eyes narrowed on them
Writing a line in a small brown leather diary held open on the felt in front of him, a pencil in his right hand, eyes down, spectacles on
Touching the crucifix: two fingers of his right hand resting on the small silver crucifix at his collar, eyes lowered for a moment; left arm as at rest
C: Checking a pocket: his right hand patting the front of his coat at the chest, a bulb of garlic just peeking out of the pocket, a small knowing look
Muttering aside: his head turned a little toward the left of the picture, mouth moving out of one corner, brows knitted; arms as at rest
Sniffing the air, frowning: his chin lifted, nose up, brows drawn together, eyes half closed; arms as at rest
Glancing at the fireplace over his right shoulder, toward the left of the picture, eyes wary; arms as at rest
Peering at the viewer over the top of his spectacles, head tipped down a little, brows raised; arms as at rest
Settling his spectacles back up his nose with one finger of his right hand
D: Talking: his right index finger raised, lecturing, mouth open mid-word
Facing a big bet: brows drawn right down, studying, mouth set; arms as at rest
Lost a pot: a heavy sigh, eyes closed, a small shake of the head; arms as at rest
A crushing loss: his spectacles pushed up onto his forehead, his right hand over his closed eyes, shoulders slumped; left arm as at rest
Down to two players: leaning in on both forearms, eyes keen behind the spectacles
A short, warm laugh, head tipped back, eyes creased shut behind the spectacles; arms as at rest

style: STYLE, the most important rule: match the SECOND attached image (the Headless Horseman, from the same table) exactly: a GOTHIC GRAPHIC-NOVEL style for a grown-up card game, halfway between a bright cartoon and a dark painted illustration. Take NOTHING of his character: no armour, no pumpkin, no cloak, no headless neck. Keep what the game needs: a bold dark outline round every shape, big clear readable shapes, a silhouette that reads at a tiny size. Adult, realistic proportions (never a big head, never chibi, never cute); shading in three or four tones with deep, dramatic shadows and a warm rim light from candlelight; rich but MUTED colour, nothing candy-bright; cloth with real weight and heavy folds; a little texture in the shadows only. Serious, weary and a little dangerous. NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute, NOT toy-like, NOT round and bouncy, NOT photoreal, NOT muddy or murky.
style_short: Keep the gothic graphic-novel style of the attached sheets and of the Headless Horseman's sheet: bold dark outlines, adult proportions, deep three- or four-tone shading, a warm candlelit rim light, rich muted colour; serious and sombre, NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute.
